A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix reorganization. Internal inconsistencies in some v6 additions do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v5 reports original MLLM accuracy and consistency experiments, correction-method evaluations, and manual analyses of table and axes extraction.

after.justification: v6 retains those original results and adds newer-model evaluations, correction tests, and reasoning and redrawing error analyses.

M1.justification: The six correction procedures, extraction and reasoning model roles, Matplotlib redrawing, and fallback to the original visualization remain unchanged. Additional model evaluations and minor prompt wording edits do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CALVI, CHARTOM, the 42 real-world misleading cases, VLAT, ChartQA, and four Likert-scale visualization pairs, with unchanged Table 1 counts and 17 misleader categories. Added breakdowns and model tests reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v6 adds a recent-model comparison against Claude-3.5-sonnet and includes ChartGemma and GPT5-mini in correction comparisons. Two recent-model identities are inconsistently documented: Table 6 lists GPT5 and Gemini-2.5-flash, whereas Appendix C names GPT4.1 and Gemini-2.5-flash-lite. The comparator expansion is nevertheless clear; existing comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v6 extends correction evaluations to ChartGemma and GPT5-mini and adds protocols for manual reasoning and redrawing audits on random samples of 30 misleading instances. Original dataset sizes and zero-shot, temperature-zero settings remain. Newly specified accuracy rules and ChartQA score provenance clarify documentation rather than establish reruns.

E4.justification: v6 substantially expands diagnostics with question-type and paired-CHARTOM accuracy analyses, CoT reasoning-error categorization, and redrawing-quality analysis, including new case studies (Tables 4–5, 10, 13; Figures 13–15, 19–21). v5 already contained CoT performance comparisons and table/axes extraction analyses; those are retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: v6 adds bootstrap confidence intervals using 5,000 resamples for all 19 models on both principal QA datasets (Figure 4 and Table 3), where v5 reported point estimates. Experiment 2 replaces the one-sided paired t-test with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The bootstrap count does not indicate additional model runs.

E6.justification: The principal QA and correction plots retain their scores, but v6 adds substantial model, subgroup, and diagnostic results. Table 8 newly reports table-based QA changes of +27.3/+23.4 percentage points for ChartGemma and -9.1/-20.1 for GPT5-mini on misleading/non-misleading data. These are new correction evaluations, not version-to-version gains. Figure 5 estimates and Experiment 2 p-values also change, while the significance pattern remains.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and the misleader definitions remain substantively unchanged. The newly stated standard random-baseline formulas explain an existing comparator rather than introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: vulnerability of the 19-model study, coverage of 17 misleaders, comparison of six corrections, and effectiveness of table-based QA and redrawing with accuracy tradeoffs.

C2.justification: v6 explicitly treats the Likert findings as preliminary and acknowledges chart complexity and question difficulty as alternatives to the parametric-knowledge explanation. It also attributes the contrasting ChartGemma/GPT5-mini correction outcomes to model capabilities and adds interpretations of reasoning and redrawing failures. These refine the retained vulnerability and mitigation account.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 newly specifies exact-match evaluation, 5% tolerance for numerical free-text answers, random-baseline calculations, and provenance of reference ChartQA scores. v6 identifies InternVL2.5-8B as the model behind retained extraction examples and updates the advertised repository link. These are documentation and access-reference changes.

R1.justification: v6 adds the InternVL paper cited as Chen et al. (2024b) for benchmark provenance and the Gemini 2.5 technical report. The existing Chen et al. reference is retained as 2024a. The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 corrects the author byline and localized grammar, organizes implementation details under descriptive subheadings, and consolidates appendix material by experiment and analysis topic. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v6 redesigns introductory and method illustrations, adds confidence-interval bars, detailed result tables, and reasoning/redrawing case figures, and regroups appendix displays. Retained heatmap and CoT plots are renumbered. New display errors include Figure 3 changing the redrawn answer from True to False while marking it correct, and mismatched captions in Figures 19–21.

improvement.justification: Compared with v5, confidence intervals, broader diagnostics, and the GPT5-mini correction failures improve assessment of uncertainty and applicability. More cautious interpretations also help. These gains are partly offset by inconsistent model identities in Table 6 versus Appendix C, counts mislabeled as percentages in Tables 10 and 13, and incorrect figure labels. The retained core evidence remains useful, but these reporting errors limit the overall quality gain.
